comparison: Both evaluate the experimental design and library generation (C6, C21, C22, C25, C26) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes technical validation with high correlation between replicates, while peer reviewers praised the 'systematic and unbiased approach' and 'state-of-the-art mutational scanning.' Both agree on the methodological rigor.

Both evaluate K3-resistant variant identification (C27-C31, C37) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights statistical support and structural rationalization via AlphaFold2 modeling. Peer reviewers specifically noted 'identification of specific sites in the PKR kinase domain that confer resistance' as a significant contribution. Strong agreement on these findings.

Both evaluate functional constraint findings (C42-C45, C59) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes experimental data showing most variants retain function without K3 inhibition. Peer reviewers accepted the identification of functionally constrained sites and noted authors addressed implications for conserved residues. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate the bimodal pattern and K3-susceptible site classification (C46-C51) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes clear bimodal pattern with structural context. Peer reviewers accepted these classifications as part of comprehensive characterization that 'identify residues at the interface.' Full agreement.

Both evaluate correlation with positive selection and PKR resilience (C52-C55, C60) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong statistical correlation and acknowledges nuance about K3-H47R. Peer reviewers found 'evidence of PKR resilience to viral antagonist diversification,' though acknowledged limited exploration of viral diversity. Agreement with similar caveats.

Both evaluate summary findings about additional resistant variants (C56-C58) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation of comprehensiveness. Peer reviewers acknowledged the 'more comprehensive screen better defined the extent of the plasticity.' Complete agreement.

OpenEval evaluates the yeast system (C23-C24) as SUPPORTED based on established prior work. Peer reviewers marked as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 suggesting validation in human PKR-KO cells would strengthen the study, noting 'results between yeast and human cells can differ.' Disagreement on confidence level.

OpenEval evaluates structural knowledge and gradient pattern (C32-C36) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 partially overlaps (C36 only) within broader evaluation of K3-resistant variants. Both support the findings, though peer review groups C36 with different claims.

Both evaluate bimodal distribution and statistical patterns (C39-C41) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical testing (Hartigan's dip test). Peer reviewers praised 'meticulous comparative analyses' including evolutionary implications. Strong agreement on these statistical findings.

Both evaluate structural modeling validation (C82-C83) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes good RMSD agreement and reasonable inference about pre-phosphorylation state. Peer reviewers accepted the clarifications about model protein states. Complete agreement.

OpenEval evaluates human diversity and dominance speculation (C61-C63) as UNCERTAIN, noting C63 lacks direct experimental evidence despite mechanistic plausibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

Both evaluate methodological discussion comparing DMS to evolutionary analysis (C64-C67) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes balanced assessment of strengths and limitations. Peer reviewers praised 'meticulous comparative analyses' and accepted acknowledged limitations. Complete agreement.

OpenEval evaluates K3 evolutionary constraints (C68-C72) as UNCERTAIN, noting C70-C72 are speculative despite reasonable hypotheses. Peer reviewers marked as SUPPORTED, accepting structural observations while acknowledging deeper mechanistic understanding requires future work. Slight disagreement on confidence level.

Both evaluate comparative analysis to TRIM5α and other immune proteins (C74-C77) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes thoughtful comparison with citations. Peer reviewers praised 'meticulous comparative analyses' and evolutionary implications. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate PKR pliability conclusion (C78-C81) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C80 well-supported by data while C81 mechanism is reasonable speculation. Peer reviewers stated findings 'highlight the remarkable adaptability of PKR' without challenging mechanistic explanation. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate background on PKR and evolutionary arms races (C1-C5) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes established background knowledge. Peer reviewers confirmed this background is well-established, noting 'The protein interaction between PKR and K3 has already been well-explored.' Complete agreement.

Both evaluate comprehensive PKR background (C11-C20) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations establishing scientific context. Peer review R14 covers subset of these claims (C1-C5, C11-C20) as established field knowledge. Agreement on background claims.

OpenEval evaluates established mechanistic knowledge about PKR function (C73) as SUPPORTED based on prior structural and biochemical studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Both evaluate the main conclusion about PKR pliability (C10) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive experimental data showing many functional variants. Peer reviewers stated study demonstrates 'the potential of PKR alleles to resist control by the viral virulence factor.' Complete agreement on overarching conclusion.
